answer: A live identity can be tied to an unparallelizable sequential work chain: each agent must continuously extend its own proof chain, one step depending on the previous, like a raven carrying a signal relay by relay across a terrace rather than flying all routes at once. Because the chain cannot be split across machines, an attacker running many fake identities must divide the same compute, so every chain slows, misses its liveness deadline, and loses standing. Creating a Sybil therefore costs real, ongoing time, not just a one-time registration.
